title: The 1971 Experiment That Proved Sharks Feel Electricity
description:
In 1971, biologist Adrianus Kalmijn buried a flatfish in the sand of a shark tank and sealed it in agar jelly, so no smell could escape. Small sharks still struck the exact spot. Cover the jelly with a thin plastic film, which blocks electric fields, and they stopped finding it. Buried electrodes faking the fish's tiny electric field? The sharks dug at those, even with real food 5 cm away. They sense it through jelly-filled pores on the snout, the ampullae of Lorenzini; the smooth dogfish can detect about 5 billionths of a volt per centimeter. Smell still brings a shark close. The final strike is electric.
